why_relevant: Example of the Hungarian-language 'esettanulmányok' pattern used by local IT suppliers to name their financial-sector reference clients. Establishes the local search idiom (esettanulmány / referenciák / ügyfeleink) that should be applied across every HU vendor and integrator site.

source_name: ITBusiness.hu — Hungarian IT/banking trade portal (azonnali fizetés, banki rendszerek)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language IT trade portal that covers bank technology projects and frequently quotes the supplier (Capsys, T-Systems, integrators) behind an implementation — local-language confirmation that rarely appears in English vendor releases.

4iG is the largest Hungarian-owned ICT integrator and the most likely local prime contractor / reseller competitor in bank-facing infrastructure and self-service deals. Its own press release stream names contracts, partners and occasionally client institutions.
Corporate profile deck typically lists business divisions and named sector references, including financial-sector (FinTech) positioning — a compact map of what 4iG claims to hold.

source_name: Budapesti Értéktőzsde (BÉT) issuer disclosure feed — 4iG Nyrt.
why_relevant: 4iG is listed, so material contracts, acquisitions of banking-IT subsidiaries and segment revenues must be disclosed. Regulated filings are the highest-credibility view of a competitor's financial-sector business.

source_name: T-Systems Magyarország — banking solutions site (Jövő bankja / Next Generation Banking)
why_relevant: T-Systems (Magyar Telekom group) is a top-tier local integrator with a dedicated banking practice, including instant-payment and cloud/data-centre offers to banks. Its solution pages reveal the product stack it resells into Hungarian banks.

source_name: CARDNET Zrt. — Hungarian card-acceptance / POS operator
why_relevant: CARDNET is the most direct Hungarian competitor in the payment-terminal/acceptance space: it sells and operates POS terminals (BÉT profile cites >6,500 terminals) on proprietary software, and is expanding to export markets. Its site and news are the primary window on the contested acquiring/terminal accounts.

source_name: Dorsum Zrt. — Hungarian investment/banking software vendor (blog + corporate site)
why_relevant: Dorsum is the leading local ISV for securities/wealth/private-banking front and back ends, and openly discusses bank projects (e.g. a Magyar Bankholding IT implementation and migration interview). Its blog names client institutions and project scope — a direct read on which Hungarian banks a local ISV holds.

Mid-size Hungarian integrator (~80 professionals) covering ERP/CRM/BI, ITIL service management and system integration; a plausible subcontractor/competitor on bank back-office and integration work. Site is the entry point to its reference and sector pages.

source_name: NETLOCK Kft. — Hungarian qualified trust service provider
why_relevant: NETLOCK supplies qualified e-signature, e-seal and timestamp products (NETLOCK Sign Enterprise) that banks embed in branch and remote onboarding flows — directly adjacent to branch-digitisation and paperless-branch competition. Product and 'about/certifications' pages reveal its bank-facing positioning and audit status (ISO 9001, ISO 27001).

Hungarian software-engineering house active since 1991 with declared banking-IT and application-development expertise; a likely delivery subcontractor on bank projects and a source of indirect signals about which platforms are being maintained locally.
Local ISV offering eBanking products; a domestic competitor/partner candidate in digital-channel deals at smaller Hungarian banks and savings institutions.

source_name: Company registry aggregators (OPTEN, Céginfo, Nemzeti Cégtár, CompanyWall, EMIS)
why_relevant: Fast lookup of ownership, cégjegyzékszám, activity codes, credit ratings and management for every actor in the cell (Grepton, CARDNET, Sysdata, Netlock etc.), including ownership changes that signal consolidation among bank-serving integrators.

source_name: Portfolio Banking Technology conference — programme, speakers and sponsors
why_relevant: The annual Hungarian banking-IT conference. Sponsor lists and speaker affiliations are an efficient census of who is actively selling to Hungarian banks in a given year, and joint bank+vendor sessions effectively announce live accounts.

source_name: Bitport.hu — Hungarian enterprise IT trade press
why_relevant: Covers the Hungarian integrator market critically (e.g. analysis of the largest domestic system integrator, lists of centrally-approved IT suppliers), including win/loss and consolidation stories that vendor sites never publish.
Reports named integrator contracts including payment-adjacent systems (e.g. T-Systems taking on the BKK ticketing/payment system). Good for contract-award news with technical detail.

source_name: Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA / hunfintech.com) member directory
why_relevant: Membership list is a ready-made actor map of Hungarian fintech and bank-tech vendors (Dorsum among them), useful for snowballing beyond the obvious integrators into niche ISVs competing for bank budget.

source_name: MKIK 'Vállalkozz digitálisan' accredited IT supplier and product catalogue
why_relevant: Chamber-of-commerce accredited supplier registry listing Hungarian IT vendors and their approved products (Grepton appears there). A vetted, structured list for enumerating and validating local integrators.

source_name: FinTechZone — 'A Nagy Magyar FinTech Történelem' and market coverage
why_relevant: Curated history/landscape of Hungarian fintech vendors, giving founding dates, pivots and acquisitions for local ISVs — valuable context for judging which local competitors are durable versus fading.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) — glossary and publications
why_relevant: Sector body whose glossary, position papers and conference materials fix the correct Hungarian terminology (pénzintézet, hitelintézet, elszámolásforgalom) needed for precise local-language querying, and whose events list bank-side IT decision makers.

source_subtype: business/financial trade press — sector tag feed
why_relevant: Hungary's leading financial-business daily; covers bank strategy, IT budgets, digital transformation and frequently names technology vendors and integrators in reconstructed deal stories that neither bank nor vendor announces formally.

Hungarian enterprise-IT trade title that writes named bank deployment stories (vendor + reseller/integrator + bank), which is exactly the leakage channel for private-bank procurement. Confirmed examples name OTP with Hitachi Data Systems and reseller Invigor Informatika, and cover AFR/instant payments and DÁP eID rollouts.

Profiles Hungarian fintechs and their bank client rosters — e.g. reporting that FintechX works with MKB, CIB, Gránit Bank, Takarékbank and Cherrisk. Client-list journalism is one of the few open ways to map private-bank vendor relationships.

MNB-adjacent economic portal that translates the central bank's digitalisation/fintech reports into narrative pieces on which banks are digitally advanced and where their internal systems lag — useful as a demand-side signal for vendor targeting.
Hungarian bank-technology trade show whose exhibitor/speaker roster is a direct enumeration of the vendor landscape addressing HU banks; case sessions surface reference customers.
Community/industry portal covering bank-fintech cooperation and competition; event recaps name which institutions are piloting with which fintechs.

Long-running Hungarian IT magazine (since 1999) with an IT/Tech section that reports outages, platform migrations and technology incidents affecting banks — incident coverage often exposes which supplier's system a bank actually runs.

source_subtype: ICT news portal / PR wire hybrid
why_relevant: One of the oldest Hungarian vertical IT news portals; carries a high volume of vendor and integrator press releases, including bank-project announcements that never reach mainstream press. Low editorial filtering makes it a good raw feed of supplier claims.
